blocks.text: A capacitor is a device to store charge. Alternatively, it is possible to think of a capacitor as a device for storing electrical energy. After all the charge on the plates possesses electrical potential energy which arises because work is to be done to deposit charge on the plates.

A good evidence of the energy stored in a charged capacitor is that of its discharging. If we connects the plates of charged capacitor by means of a thick wire, the charge flows from one plate to the other to neutralize the opposite charge on it. As a result, the wire becomes hot. Since heat is a form of energy, so the capacitor possessed energy when it was charged, and it was this energy which appeared as heat.

Therefore if we draw a V vs Q graph, it will be a straight line passing through the origin as shown in Fig. 16.10. In fact, with each small increment of charge deposited during the charging process, the potential difference between the plates increases, and a larger amount of work is needed to bring up next increment of charge.

Therefore total work done to charge the capacitor to a final value Q is equal to the sum of areas of all such rectangles under V vs Q graph. blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The question states a 100 V supply, but the solution uses 120 V. With the stated 100 V: Q = C_eV = (8/3 × 10⁻⁶ F)(100 V) = 2.67 × 10⁻⁴ C and W = ½QV = ½(2.67 × 10⁻⁴ C)(100 V) = 1.33 × 10⁻² J. The printed 3.2 × 10⁻⁴ C and 1.92 × 10⁻² J hold only for a 120 V supply.

blocks.title: Example 16.8
blocks.problem: A 16μF capacitor is charged to a potential difference of 100V. Determine the energy stored in it. If the potential difference is doubled by what factor does the energy increase?
steps:
Energy stored is given by;
W = ½CV²

Putting the values of C and V, we get
W = ½(16 × 10⁻⁶ F) × (100)²

blocks.text: Since energy depends on V², therefore if V² is doubled, the energy increases by a factor (2)², i.e., energy increases by 4 times.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: It is the potential difference V that is doubled, as the question says. Since W ∝ V², doubling V increases the energy by a factor (2)² = 4. If V² itself were doubled, the energy would only double.
